metadata.title: Nvidia, AMD, Micron Lead Chip Stocks Selloff as Iran Tensions Rattle Markets

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and other major semiconductor stocks dipped Tuesday as renewed uncertainty around U.S.-Iran negotiations pressured the broader market and weighed on technology shares.
Nvidia fell about 2% after committing more than $100 billion in credit support for an OpenAI data center project in Ohio. The company will also invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy, which is developing the facility.
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) declined about 3% as investors weighed reports that Google (GOOG) is working with AMD on a future tensor processing unit. Wedbush said such a development could alter the competitive landscape for AI chips.
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) dropped about 2%, while Micron Technology (MU) sank nearly 4% as memory stocks came under pressure. The sector has faced swings as investors assess AI infrastructure spending and the potential returns from large capital commitments.
Alphabet was also under pressure, with Google shares among technology stocks affected by the broader market decline. The Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 1.38%, while the S&P 500 slipped about 0.59%.
What it means for stocks: The selloff highlights near-term pressure on AI and semiconductor shares as geopolitical uncertainty adds to concerns surrounding elevated AI investment.
